executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 indicate multiple concurrent disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated multiple epidemiological updates in the Americas region, representing a persistent zoonotic threat with pandemic potential. Mpox, dengue, yellow fever, measles, and chikungunya are simultaneously circulating in the Americas, while ECDC weekly reports suggest ongoing European communicable disease activity. The convergence of respiratory pathogens including seasonal influenza, RSV, and pertussis further strains public health response capacity across both hemispheres.
bottomLine: Multiple concurrent epidemic threats—most critically Avian Influenza A(H5N1) as a BSL-3 select agent—are active across the Americas and Europe, requiring coordinated surveillance and response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing zoonotic activity
Persistent animal-to-human spillover risk warranting BSL-3 classification and heightened pandemic preparedness
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance protocols, ensure antiviral stockpile readiness, monitor for human-to-human transmission clusters, and coordinate with FAO and OIE on animal reservoir controls

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating ongoing transmission in the Americas
Sustained viral circulation following 2022-2023 global outbreak with potential clade diversification risk
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination programs, monitor for emerging clade variants, and ensure diagnostic capacity across member states

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active cases or outbreak risk
Sylvatic transmission cycles ongoing with risk of urban spillover in under-vaccinated populations
threats.action: Expand vaccination coverage in at-risk regions, enhance entomological surveillance, and reinforce traveler vaccination requirements

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 indicating elevated case counts
Seasonal amplification patterns consistent with high-transmission period across tropical and subtropical zones
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations, activate dengue case management protocols, and monitor serotype shifts that may increase severe disease risk

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active transmission or importation risk
Vaccination coverage gaps identified post-COVID-19 pandemic creating susceptible cohorts
threats.action: Conduct urgent vaccination gap assessments, implement catch-up immunization campaigns, and strengthen outbreak investigation capacity

threats.name: Pertussis
signals: Two PAHO updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained or resurging transmission
Cyclical epidemic pattern with potential waning immunity and vaccine hesitancy contributing to resurgence
threats.action: Review booster vaccination schedules for adolescents and adults, ensure maternal Tdap coverage, and enhance laboratory confirmation capacity

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active circulation
Co-circulation with dengue virus in overlapping Aedes mosquito vector territories complicates clinical differentiation
threats.action: Enhance arboviral syndromic surveillance, implement integrated vector management, and ensure clinical guidance distinguishes chikungunya from dengue for case management

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating active cases or elevated risk
Rodent reservoir activity associated with environmental and seasonal conditions driving spillover events
threats.action: Strengthen rodent control programs in high-risk rural communities, enhance public awareness campaigns, and ensure critical care capacity for severe pulmonary cases

selectAgentSummary: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is a BSL-3 select agent detected with multiple epidemiological updates in the Americas region (November 2025 and March 2026). This pathogen poses significant zoonotic and pandemic risk. Yellow fever virus is also classified as a BSL-3 select agent, with an active PAHO alert issued March 2026 for the Americas. Both pathogens require heightened biosafety containment, international notification protocols, and coordinated One Health response frameworks.

diseases: Communicable disease threats (multiple, ECDC weekly reports)

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis strains with macrolide resistance markers warrant monitoring given resurgence signals in the Americas
No explicit AMR reports identified in current surveillance titles; ongoing vigilance recommended for dengue co-infections treated empirically with antibiotics
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever) in the Americas creating diagnostic and response burden
Dual-hemisphere influenza and RSV activity with overlapping seasons increasing healthcare system pressure
Recurring PAHO alerts suggest sustained public health infrastructure stress following COVID-19 pandemic recovery
Mpox persistence in the Americas post-2022 outbreak indicates endemic establishment rather than contained epidemic
Multiple ECDC weekly threat reports spanning April-May 2026 suggest active European surveillance of emerging communicable disease signals
